entry_points.text: Die observer ignores non-user or kernel traps, claims breakpoints on pre-step and debug events on post-step.
Legacy entry forwards image non-extended; multiplexed entry answers install probe and forwards enter extended.

Entry is 64-bit startup relative to load (32-bit analogue); text, rodata, data, diagnostics, init, no-save, bss, bootstrap order with large alignment, RX text, RW data, link checks, size bound, mitigation spacing, 64KiB slop.
Restart leaves long mode via low table with paging off, loads real-mode tables, fills segments and far-transfers with caches written back.

Wake entry repairs segments, sets stack and tables, verifies signatures then calls C main with spin on bad magic and error on bad signature; restores misc, base, CR4, EFER per bits, loads GDT and jumps via starter or to 64-bit trampoline.

exports.text: Uprobe helpers report XOL trap mismatch, skip step via emulate hook signalling trap, and detect entry by frame byte or 64-bit terminator.
Hijack reads user stack per width, skips replaced slots, installs trampoline, syncs shadow stack; failure forces fault signal.
Crash info records paging facts on 32-bit; on 64-bit also base, top table, level, relocation, size and encryption mask.
Defaults group resource, firmware, irq, timer, IOMMU, PCI, hypervisor, ACPI with silent noops, parallel bringup and native ops; silent wallclock fallback; 1MB limit.

hazards.text: XOL allocation briefly advertises compat status for limited cases then clears it.
VM86 stack uses byte user accesses adjusting pointer per unit, composing wider values, diverting to failure on fault.

invariants.text: VM86 flags have full and short views; updates use masks and track interrupt bit.
Return probe liveness uses strict stack comparison after call entry and inclusive elsewhere.
Trampoline is non-executable, then prefix is read-only with text executable.
Real-mode image exports base, entry, ro-end, video bounds and far-jump helper; header, rodata with video table, page-aligned code/data, bss, signature.

locks.text: VM86 routes irq management to handler; 16 lines pair owner and signal with bitmap under spin lock; atomic test-clear reenables only if set; ownership, privilege and allowed signals enforced.
AP trampoline lock is published cleared as unlocked.

state_machines.text: XOL completion restores trap, runs post hook with fault-address fallback, signals single-step and clears local step; abort restores similarly.
Early CPU check preserves flags, records vendor, clears execute-disable inhibit on Intel, enforces masks with one AMD retry; zero means success.
VM86 entry is one-shot, needs low-memory permission, rejects reentry and obsolete option, captures registers, derives flags with class-dependent writability and presents image as trap frame.
VM86 faults skip prefixes, emulate flag and far-return ops, dispatch software interrupts, toggle virtual interrupt, and exit on irq, forced return, trace, unknown op or fault.

Trampoline keeps header pointer; goes from low reservation to copy, relocation and publication with EFER sanitize, CR4 snapshot, identity and kernel mappings plus encryption tweaks; missing header fails boot; late hook delegates via platform vector.
32-bit secondary writes back caches, blocks interrupts, loads target, installs null IDT via wide loads, enables protection and forwards via starter; null-IDT faults shut down.

64-bit secondary blocks interrupts, checks long mode with halt on failure, installs tables and enters protected mode; protected stage restores CR4, top table, EFER with SME then pages; direct entry continues or toggles depth via compat then jumps to kernel virtual address; confidential entry skips cache and check.

structs.text: Safe mask 0xDD5, return mask 0xDFF, irq name vm86irq.
Resume header packs video, pmode entry/cs/controls/efer/gdt/misc/behavior/flags/magic/signature; offset 8 expects 0x51ee1111 with misc/CR4/EFER restore bits.
Main spins on bad magic 0x12345678, runs Morse test, BIOS call and video probe per flags; Morse maps dots, dashes, gaps to timed tones; speaker uses 1193181/frequency via 0x43, 0x42, 0x61.
